stats.privacyNote: Microphone, camera and screen are encrypted in this browser before they reach the server, which forwards them without being able to read them. A compromised server could still interfere with who holds the keys, and who speaks when stays visible to it. Chat and attachments stay readable by the server, and nothing is recorded.

If it matches everywhere, everyone holds the same keys with exactly the members listed. It changes whenever someone joins or leaves. A name in red holds the keys without being in this Talk, or holds them twice. Only the code is end-to-end: the names come from the server.

legal.title: Legal & privacy notice
legal.subtitle: Transparency, data protection (Art. 13 GDPR) and terms of use for Mnema Talk

operator.heading: 1. Operator & controller
operator.introAfter: is a private, non-commercial software project for closed communities – with no profit motive, no advertising revenue and no business relationship. Accounts are issued only through personal invite codes.

privacy.heading: 2. Privacy notice under Art. 13 GDPR
privacy.introBefore: Your privacy and data sovereignty come first. Only the technical minimum needed for reliable chat, voice and video is collected. Your data is
privacy.introStrong: never sold, never passed on to advertisers and never used to train AI models
privacy.basisConsent: : By registering and using your invite code you consent to your profile data and uploaded media being stored.
privacy.basisContractTitle: Performance of a contract / terms of use (Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR)
privacy.basisContract: : To provide the chat and voice service, authentication and session management.
privacy.basisInterest: : Short-lived error and access logs to protect against abuse and brute-force attacks.
privacy.voiceHeading: WebRTC voice, video & screen sharing: 100% routed through the server
privacy.voiceBefore: Unlike typical chat apps, Mnema Talk runs a dedicated
privacy.voiceNoP2p: There are no direct peer-to-peer connections between participants.
privacy.voiceAfter1: Your IP address is therefore never disclosed to other people in a Talk. Audio streams and screen shares are forwarded selectively in real time in memory and
privacy.voiceNoRecord: are never recorded or stored permanently
privacy.stunBefore: To set up the voice connection, your browser asks the following STUN servers for your public address:
privacy.stunAfter: . Your IP address is sent to the operator of each of these servers; no conversation or message content is transmitted.
privacy.updateCheck: About every 30 minutes the server asks GitHub (api.github.com, GitHub Inc., USA) whether a new version of Mnema Talk was released. GitHub only sees the server’s IP address; no user data is sent. The operator can turn the check off.
privacy.noStun: No external STUN or TURN servers from third parties are used.
privacy.mediaPurpose: Images, documents and avatars in the local S3 storage
privacy.sessionRetention: Up to {days} days or until you sign out
privacy.moderationPurpose: Reports, automod entries and private notes that moderators keep about members; never part of a data export
privacy.moderationRetention: Until the moderators delete them; entries about a deleted account stay under “Deleted member”
privacy.rightsHeading: Your rights as a data subject
privacy.rights1Before: Under Art. 15–22 GDPR you have the right at any time, free of charge, to
privacy.rights1Mid5: . To exercise these rights, simply email
privacy.rights2Before: You may also object to processing based on legitimate interests (Art. 21 GDPR) and withdraw any consent you gave at any time with effect for the future (Art. 7(3) GDPR). You also have the right to
privacy.rightsComplain: lodge a complaint with a data protection supervisory authority
privacy.rights2After: (Art. 77 GDPR), in particular in the country where you live or where the operator is based.
privacy.noiseFilter: AI noise suppression (DeepFilterNet3 or GTCRN) runs entirely in your browser. Your microphone signal is not sent to any third party for it; the model and code come from this server.
privacy.selfService: Without emailing anyone: under Account & security in the account menu you can download a copy of your data (JSON files in a ZIP, once per day) and delete your account yourself. Deleting erases your profile, avatar, e-mail address, sessions and uploads; your messages stay in their threads as written by “Deleted member” without their text. An optional e-mail address is used only to confirm it and to reset your password, and is never shown to other members.

cookies.heading: 3. Cookies & local storage
cookies.body: Mnema Talk does not use marketing, tracking or third-party cookies. In line with § 25(2) TDDDG, only strictly necessary session data (the sign-in cookie) and local settings (for example microphone level and noise gate thresholds) are stored in your browser. A cookie banner is therefore not legally required.

terms.heading: 4. Terms of use
terms.use: The platform is for private conversation. Users agree not to share unlawful, insulting, inciting or copyright-infringing content.
terms.liabilityBefore: Because this is a free, private spare-time project, it is provided “as is” (
terms.liabilityAfter: ) with no guarantee of permanent availability or freedom from errors.
terms.rules: The operator may suspend accounts without prior notice in cases of serious disrespect or threats to the security of the infrastructure.

oss.heading: 5. Open-source credits
oss.intro: Mnema Talk is free software itself (GNU AGPL-3.0) and is built on free software. Here is everything we use and ship to you, with its license.

trusted_proxy_broad.title: TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS is too broad
trusted_proxy_broad.body: It contains broad ranges while the server is reachable beyond loopback. Any host in those ranges can forge its client address and evade rate limits and the sign-in lock. List only your reverse proxy’s address.

proxy_not_trusted.title: Requests arrive through an untrusted proxy
proxy_not_trusted.body: Requests came in through a proxy that is not in TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS, so all clients share one rate-limit identity. Add the reverse proxy’s address to TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS.

webrtc_reachability.title: Voice may not work outside this host
webrtc_reachability.body: Neither WEBRTC_NAT_1TO1_IP nor WEBRTC_TURN_URLS is set, so browsers are told the container’s own address. Set WEBRTC_NAT_1TO1_IP to the public (and LAN) address, or add a TURN server.

webrtc_udp_mux_disabled.title: Voice capacity is limited
webrtc_udp_mux_disabled.body: WEBRTC_UDP_MUX_PORT=0 gives every media peer its own UDP port from the range ({count} ports), which caps how many people can be in calls at once. Leave it empty to share one port.

insecure_public_url.title: PUBLIC_URL is not https
insecure_public_url.body: Session cookies are sent without the Secure flag and the __Host- prefix, so someone on the network path can read or replace them. Set PUBLIC_URL to the https:// address people open, behind a reverse proxy that terminates TLS.

roles.managedHint: Managed role: held by every bot, cannot be removed.
roles.managedNote: The Bot role is managed. Every bot holds it automatically and nobody else can; it cannot be renamed, removed from a bot or deleted. You can change its colour, position and whether it is listed separately. It starts with no permissions: a bot can do nothing until you grant it something here or in a channel. Only the Owner can make bots elevated, and nobody can give bots permissions they lack themselves.
roles.title: Roles
roles.intro: Roles give members permissions. A higher role outranks a lower one. The Owner always has every permission and cannot be restricted.
roles.everyoneHint: What every member has. Roles add to it.
roles.hoist: List members of this role separately
roles.deleteBody: Everyone who has it loses it, and its channel permissions are removed.
roles.reorderHint: Drag roles or use the arrows to change their rank. Higher roles outrank lower ones.
roles.locked: This role is not below your highest role. You can look at it, but not change it.
roles.empty: No roles yet. Create one to give members more permissions.
roles.cannotGrant: You can only grant permissions you have yourself.
roles.reorderFailed: Couldn’t change the order. Try again.
roles.uploadHint: Leave empty to use the global limit. A member gets the highest limit of their roles, never above the server maximum.
roles.uploadInvalid: Enter a whole number of MB, or leave it empty.
roles.botRoleHint: Managed role of one bot: it cannot be removed.
roles.botRoleNote: “{name}” is a bot’s own role. It is created with the bot, follows its name and is deleted with it; only that bot holds it, and it cannot be renamed, given to anyone else, removed from the bot or deleted by hand. You can change its colour and permissions. Nobody can give a bot permissions they lack themselves, and only the Owner can make a bot elevated.

memberRoles.own: You cannot change your own roles.

overwrites.privateHint: Deny viewing for @everyone. Then allow it for the roles that should see this.
overwrites.loadFailed: Couldn’t load the permissions. Try again.
overwrites.ownerNote: The Owner always has access and is not listed.

webhooks.title: Webhooks of #{name}
webhooks.incomingHint: An incoming webhook gives scripts and services a secret URL to post messages into this channel with the settings below. Anyone with the URL can post, so treat it like a password.
webhooks.outgoingHint: An outgoing webhook sends events of this channel to a URL, signed so you can check they come from here. It keeps sending until an administrator changes or deletes it.
webhooks.urlOnce: Copy the URL now: it is shown only once. If it gets lost, make a new one.
webhooks.secretOnce: Copy the secret now: it is shown only once. Use it to check the signature of each delivery.
webhooks.emptyIncoming: No incoming webhooks in this channel yet.

webhooks.deleteBody: Its URL stops working at once. Messages it posted stay.

moderation.timeoutBody: They can read, but not write, react, speak, share video or join Talks until the time is up. A Talk they are in ends for them.

moderation.deleteLatest: Delete latest messages of this member…
moderation.slowModeHint: Members wait this long between two messages. Members with Manage messages are exempt.

moderation.slowModeTooLong: Slow mode can last 24 hours at most.

bots.title: Bots
bots.intro: Bots are accounts for programs: they post messages, answer slash commands and react to events through the bot API (see the bot documentation). A new bot can do nothing until you give it a role, allow its intents and issue a token. Every change here lands in the audit log.
bots.select: Pick a bot to manage it.
bots.created: Bot created. It has no access yet.
bots.disabledHint: A disabled bot is rejected at once, with all its tokens and connections. Its messages stay.
bots.deleteBody: All its tokens stop working at once and its commands disappear. Messages it posted stay.

intents.title: Allowed intents
intents.hint: What the bot is allowed to ask for when it connects to the gateway. Without an intent it receives no such events.

guilds.name: Channel changes
guilds.desc: Channels and categories being created, changed or deleted.

members.name: Members
members.desc: The member list and new members joining.

reactions.name: Reactions
reactions.desc: Reactions added to or removed from messages.

roles.managed: Managed: every bot holds this role and it cannot be taken away.
roles.title: Roles
roles.hint: A bot does not get @everyone, so it starts with no access at all. Give it roles for what it may do server-wide, and set channel access in each channel’s permissions dialog by allowing one of the bot’s roles there.
roles.empty: There are no roles yet. Create one in the Roles tab.
roles.power: Gives the bot administrator power. Only the Owner may assign this role.
roles.powerSelected: A selected role gives the bot administrator power. Only hand this to a program you fully trust.
roles.managedOwn: Managed: this is the bot’s own role and it cannot be taken away.

access.title: Effective access
access.elevated: This bot holds Administrator or admin-area permission. It can change the server far beyond messaging.

tokens.title: Tokens
tokens.hint: The bot sends a token as Authorization: Bot <token>. Only the last four characters are kept here.
tokens.name: Name (optional)

binding.unboundHint: Issued before 1.0, so no issuer is recorded. It keeps working and is bound to the bot’s creator (or the Owner) the first time it is used. Regenerate it to bind it to its real issuer.
binding.inferredHint: Issued before 1.0. On first use it was bound to the bot’s creator or the Owner, and it stops when that person loses the right to manage this bot. Regenerate it to bind it to its real issuer.

tokens.regenerateBody: The old token stops working at once. A new secret is shown once.
tokens.revokeBody: Programs using this token are rejected from now on. This cannot be undone.

secret.title: Token for {name}

twoFactor.title: Two-factor sign-in
twoFactor.intro: After your password, sign-in asks for a six-digit code from an authenticator app. A stolen password alone is then not enough.
twoFactor.recommendOwner: You are the Owner: this account can do everything. Turning on two-factor sign-in is strongly recommended.

twoFactor.proof: Enter your password and a current code from the app, or one unused recovery code.

twoFactor.fileHeader: Mnema Talk recovery codes. Each works once.
twoFactor.saved: I have stored these codes safely.

privacy.title: Your data
privacy.exportTitle: Download a copy of your data
privacy.exportIntro: A ZIP of JSON files with your profile, settings, roles, messages, reactions, uploads and the log entries about your account. It contains nothing of other members. One per day; you can download it once within 24 hours.

privacy.exportExpired: The last export expired and was removed.

privacy.deleteOwner: The Owner account cannot be deleted: ownership cannot be transferred, so the community would be left without an Owner.

automod.title: Automod
automod.hint: Rules that check every new or edited message and every sign-up. A hit is blocked or only flagged, and always appears in Reports, marked Automod. The Owner and Administrators are never held back by a rule.

about.words: Blocks or flags messages that contain one of these words or phrases. Whole words only; capitals do not matter.
about.links: Blocks or flags messages with links: every link, every link except to the allowed domains, or only links to the listed domains.
about.mentions: Blocks or flags a message that mentions more different people than allowed.
about.new_account: Keeps accounts that have just joined from posting links or files, or from posting at all, for a while.
about.raid: When many accounts join in a short time, the newcomers are timed out for a while and the moderators get an alert. A moderator can lift a timeout like any other.

automod.name: Name
automod.nameHint: Shown to the member whose message is blocked, and in Reports.
automod.wordsHint: One per line. * stands for any letters or digits, so cheat* also catches cheating.
automod.domainsHint: One per line, for example example.com. A domain covers its subdomains.
automod.maxMentions: Most different mentions in one message
automod.maxMentionsHint: @all and @here count as one each. A message with more is a hit.
automod.accountAge: An account counts as new for

automod.raidHint: Every new account counts. The newcomers of that time, and everyone who joins while the raid lasts, are timed out.
